subject: Convergence problem only with robust estimators

messages.author: 56a62d12e0977fc3
messages.subject: Convergence problem only with robust estimators
parts:
Hello, I'm new to lavaan and would appreciate your help with a convergence problem I'm having.

I'm running a random-intercept cross-lagged panel model, with 3 variables cross-lagged over 3 waves of data (n=1704, df=4).

Using the default (fiml) for missing values, and ML as the estimator, the model converges with good fit and expected estimates.

I want, however, to try out robust estimators (due to skew in the data). When I select MLM (complete data only) or even MLF or MLR (which should deal with the missingness in my data), the model doesn't converge.

Any ideas as to why this might be, or what I can do to fix it?

I can post the model syntax and/or more information if it helps.

Cheers,

Russell

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Convergence problem only with robust estimators
parts:
My initial guess was right:

The model where you use se="robust.sem" uses listwise deletion, and
fails to converge.

The model where you use estimator = "MLF" also uses listwise deletion,
and fails to converge.

If you use all the data, using fiml, the model does converge. For the
'robust' version, you need to use se="robust.huber.white", together with
missing="ml". (You can also use estimator="MLR" which will imply
se="robust.huber.white")

For estimator = "MLF", you also need to add the missing="ml" flag (if
you want fiml). Note that the informatin="expected" argument will be
(silently) ignored here, as you are use first.order information instead.

Yves.
